description:
For b7<=0 ('sct only' secondary) NJOY runs the whole temperature loop a SECOND time for the secondary scatterer with alpha scaled by arat=aws/awr (leapr.f90:328, 500), saves the principal ssm via copys (402, 2468-2487), then merges in endout (3018-3030): srat=sbs/sb with sb=spr*((1+awr)/awr)^2, sbs=sps*((1+aws)/aws)^2, and ssm=srat*ssm_secondary+ssm_principal. It also swaps which Teff/Debye-Waller belongs to which scatterer (3034-3040, tempf1/dwp1=principal) and writes a second Teff TAB1 (3578-3597).

NOT needed for water: tsl-HinH2O uses b7=1 (free gas). NO deck in the registry uses b7<=0, so this path has no test oracle and porting it now would be unreachable, unverifiable code. generate_tape refuses it explicitly. File a deck that exercises it before porting.
title: njoy leapr: true mixed-moderator ssm merge (nss>0, b7<=0) is still unported

description:
From the op-ffg6 audit, 2026-08-13. API-breaking, HIGH downstream exposure. ~1-2 weeks. Depends on C1-C6. Do this LAST.

pre_built_components/ holds most of the 809 API-breaking sites. Concentrations:
  ciet_three_branch_plus_dracs/solver_functions.rs -- ciet_pri_loop_three_branch_link_up_components alone has 81
  coupled_dracs_loop_tests/pri_loop_calc_functions.rs -- 42
  dracs_loop_calc_functions_sam_tchx_calibration.rs -- 70 + 32

This is where nearly all ~499 downstream call sites land. Per crate: outram-park-digital-twin-engine 377,
tampines 43, tampines-steam-tables 40, teh-o-prke 39, nee_soon 0.
Heaviest single files:
  digital-twin-engine/src/bin/ciet_educational_simulator_v2/.../full_simulation/mod.rs   106
  .../full_simulation/archive.rs                                                          98
  .../nat_circ_simulation/mod.rs                                                           75

DUPLICATION MULTIPLIER: examples/fhr_sim_v*/app/thermal_hydraulics_backend/mod.rs exists in FOUR near-identical copies
(34 call sites each) across tampines, digital-twin-engine, teh-o-prke and tampines-steam-tables. Fixing one means fixing
four. Consider whether that duplication should be resolved first -- it may be cheaper than doing the same edit 4x.

QUESTION FOR THE MAINTAINER, worth answering before starting: several of these CIET loop-solver functions read as
CALIBRATION SCRIPTS that simply are not #[cfg(test)]-gated. If they do not belong in the published library surface,
gating them removes both the API-breakage and the downstream churn at a stroke. That is a scoping decision, not an
engineering one.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
MAINTAINER DECISION, 2026-08-13: 'for ciet loop-solver calibration, just gate them under cfg test.'

So the open question on this bead is ANSWERED -- the CIET loop-solver / calibration functions in pre_built_components/
get #[cfg(test)] gating rather than a Result-returning API conversion. That removes both the API breakage and nearly all
the downstream churn from this bead at a stroke, since those functions are where the bulk of the ~500 downstream call
sites land.

Targets named by the audit:
  ciet_three_branch_plus_dracs/solver_functions.rs (ciet_pri_loop_three_branch_link_up_components alone has 81 sites)
  coupled_dracs_loop_tests/pri_loop_calc_functions.rs (42)
  dracs_loop_calc_functions_sam_tchx_calibration.rs (70 + 32)

CARE REQUIRED WHEN GATING -- verify before, not after:
  1. Confirm each function is genuinely only used by tests/examples before gating it. Gating something a downstream
     LIBRARY consumes turns a compile error into a missing symbol at integration time.
  2. The audit found ~499 downstream call sites, 95%+ in examples/ and src/bin/ rather than downstream lib code.
     #[cfg(test)] does NOT make an item visible to examples/ or src/bin/ -- those are separate compilation units and see
     only the normal public API. So anything an EXAMPLE or a BIN uses cannot simply be #[cfg(test)]-gated; it needs a
     different answer (feature gate, or move into the example). Check this per function; do not assume.
  3. Heaviest example/bin consumers: digital-twin-engine/src/bin/ciet_educational_simulator_v2/.../full_simulation/mod.rs
     (106), .../full_simulation/archive.rs (98), .../nat_circ_simulation/mod.rs (75).
  4. The four near-identical copies of examples/fhr_sim_v*/app/thermal_hydraulics_backend/mod.rs (34 sites each) still
     apply.

This bead's priority can drop once the gating lands, since the remaining API-breaking surface shrinks a lot.

title: C7 TUAS: pre-built components -- the bulk, ~500 downstream call sites. DO LAST.

description:
MAINTAINER REQUEST 2026-08-11: once the HTR-10 multifidelity neutronics pipeline lands, wire it into the outram-blender port.

THE PIPELINE: rigorous Monte Carlo -> MGXS -> deterministic multiphysics -> PRKE + decay heat. Each rung trades fidelity for speed and is validated against the rung above it. Scoped under op-jyyp (HTR-10 simulator); the scoping document is docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md.

WHY BLENDER IS THE RIGHT HOME. crates/outram-blender is the mesh-authoring frontend and ALREADY carries exactly this pattern twice over:
- an opt-in Monte Carlo bridge: mc-export -> sim -> MC Studio
- an OpenFOAM volume-meshing bridge: foam-mesh -> foam_mesh -> tet-dual Mesh Studio
The multifidelity pipeline becomes a THIRD bridge of the same shape — author the geometry, then drive the fidelity ladder from it. The existing MC bridge is the closest precedent and should be read first; rung 1 of the pipeline is the same Monte Carlo engine that bridge already targets, so this may extend that bridge rather than sit beside it. Decide which and record why.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT ALREADY COMMUNICATED UPSTREAM. The pipeline agent has been told to give the pipeline a HEADLESS, SCRIPTABLE entry point taking a geometry description plus a run configuration, rather than something only callable from a test — precisely so a frontend can drive it. If that constraint was not honoured, fixing the pipeline API is in scope here before wrapping it.

REPRODUCIBILITY CARRIES THROUGH THE BRIDGE. The pipeline must emit a run manifest recording the workspace commit, cross-section data and version, MC seed and batch counts, group structure and homogenisation choice. A frontend that drives the pipeline must PRESERVE and surface that manifest rather than hiding it behind a button — a result a user cannot trace back to its inputs is not usable as evidence. Same discipline as the graph digitiser bead op-5v5.8, which must record calibration with every export.

BLOCKED UNTIL THE PIPELINE LANDS. Do not start this before the rungs exist. Filed now so the intent is not lost, and so the pipeline is designed with a frontend consumer in mind rather than retrofitted.

Note outram-blender is GPL-3.0, a fork of Blender mesh architecture, and is NOT affiliated with the Blender Foundation — keep that framing intact in any docs added here.
title: outram-blender: multifidelity neutronics pipeline as a third solver bridge
